titre: Ubisoft cuts jobs at major Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios as its year of layoffs continues
chapo: Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs." Read more
extrait: Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs." GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed. The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed. In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs. "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources." These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" announced by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake. Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. titre: Ubisoft : encore 166 licenciements à Montréal et Québec
chapo: Coupe, coupe et re-coupe, Ubisoft désintègre 166 postes supplémentaires dans ses studios de Montréal (Assassin's Creed Shadows) et Québec (Immortals Fenyx Rising).
extrait: Image d'illustration : Assassin's Creed Shadows | Source : Ubisoft Coupe, coupe et re-coupe, Ubisoft désintègre 166 postes supplémentaires dans ses studios de Montréal (Assassin's Creed Shadows) et Québec (Immortals Fenyx Rising). Après le plan de 100 départs volontaires en Allemagne, la fermeture de RedLynx (Trials) et la suppression de 70 postes à Singapour (Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced), ce sont désormais les studios historiques de Montréal et Québec qui sont touchés chez Ubisoft. D'après les informations de GamesIndsutry.biz, ces coupes concernent surtout des employés « dans des rôles de production et de soutien » qui sortent « de projets récemment annulés ou significativement changés ». « Ubisoft réduit ses effectifs de 166 postes à Montréal et dans la ville de Québec », confirme un communiqué transmis à GamesIndustry.biz. « Alors que notre portfolio évolue, nos besoins en termes de production changent aussi, nous demandant d'ajuster la taille de certaines équipes afin d'assurer que nos ressources sont alignées sur les priorités de la production et nos besoins business. » Selon GamesIndustry.biz, ces fermetures de postes concernent surtout les équipes assignées à Vantage Studios, la sous-entreprise constituée avec le géant chinois Tencent pour héberger les franchises Assassin's Creed, Far Cry et Rainbow Six. De quoi rappeler la cinquantaine de postes supprimés sur Assassin's Creed Hexe plus tôt dans l'année, qui, entend-on, a significativement changé de direction sous l'impulsion du nouveau patron de la franchise Jean Guesdon... Nous aurons peut-être plus d'informations ce soir, puisque le bilan trimestriel d'Ubisoft doit tomber à 18h00 heure française.
